title: Fleet Controls: scaling safeguards, explainable autoscaler decisions, and throughput guarantees panel
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement a new Fleet Controls panel focused on scaling safeguards, explicit throughput guarantees, and a human-readable audit timeline for changes. This ticket captures the product definition, success metrics, acceptance criteria, and a plan for incremental rollout. Goals: 1) Add adjustable scaling safeguards (min/max headroom, cool-down, burst caps) with sane defaults and policy templates for common workloads. 2) Surface a throughput guarantees widget that shows committed throughput vs observed, with rolling 1h/24h views and unit-cost implications. 3) Provide an explainability layer for autoscaler actions (why a scale-up/down occurred) and a change history that includes diffs, who changed what, and one-click rollback to a prior policy. Non-goal: full RBAC for policy editing (handled in separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: UI: New Fleet Controls page contains a Scaling Safeguards section with editable fields for min_instances, max_instances, headroom_percent, cooldown_seconds, and burst_capacity. Defaults described in UX spec.
UI: Throughput Guarantees widget displays committed units, 1h/24h actual throughput, and estimated cost delta for current configuration.

Explainability: Each autoscaler decision in the last 7 days can be inspected showing metrics that triggered the action (CPU/GPU utilization, token backlog, latency SLO breach), the evaluated policies, and the fallback used.
Audit: Change history is searchable, shows config diffs, user, timestamp, and links to related PR/Confluence notes. Rollback button reverts active policy and emits an audit entry.
Telemetry: Backend exposes new metrics and events (autoscaler.action, policy.change, throttle.applied) and example Grafana dashboards included in the PR.
E2E: Integration test that simulates burst traffic and validates that safeguards prevent overprovisioning beyond configured max_instances and that rollback returns the fleet to prior state.
Docs: Console help text and one-pager for SREs + short video walkthrough in docs site.
Security: Policy edits require a console user with policy-editor scope; ticket to wire RBAC is tracked separately.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: synchronous explanation generation increases decision latency; we chose async generation stored with action events so operators can inspect without impacting SLOs.
Policy templates to include: steady-state SaaS, bursty short-lived queries, and latency-sensitive with high headroom. Templates to be editable and saved per-fleet.
Design constraint: minimize vertical screen space for operators on-call. Desktop does full history view, mobile shows most recent 3 entries and a rollback CTA.
Metrics/queries: Suggested PromQL for committed vs observed throughput (provided in Confluence doc).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API & Telemetry): Add event schema, autoscaler.action event, and policy.change events. ENG to expose read APIs for recent actions.
Phase 2 (UI - Safeguards + Guarantees): Implement UI bindings, templates, and throughput guarantees widget. Enable read-only rollout to 10% of orgs for feedback.
Phase 3 (Explainability + Audit): Persist explanations, implement history UI with diffs and rollback, add E2E tests.
Rollout: Canary to internal fleets -> beta customers (opt-in) -> general availability. Collect customer feedback and adjust default templates.
Rollback plan: feature flag for UI + API; rollback UI only does not affect autoscaler behavior. Full rollback requires reversion of API schema changes tracked in ENG-48900.
